headline: Nəsimi: Central district with high transport access and dense commercial amenities

tags.reason: The transport index is 79, backed by 5 metro stations and 145 bus stops.
Commercial property prices stand at AZN 3,692/m² with 15 shopping malls available.

summary: Nəsimi is a dense central district of Baku with a population of 219,700 and a density of 21,970 people per km². It features high urban infrastructure, with 100% of known roads paved, although 34.7% of the surface data remains unknown. The neighbourhood offers 14.29 food establishments and 6.55 grocery stores per 10,000 residents. Property prices are sample-based, with new apartments priced at AZN 2,660/m² and old apartments at AZN 2,385/m².
strengths: Transport index is significantly above median at 79, compared to the Baku median of 56 (neqliyyat index 79; median 56).
Infrastructure index reaches 96 with 100% of known road surfaces paved (infrastruktur index 96; median 49).
Bank and ATM density is high at 6.87 per 10,000 residents, compared to the national median of 2.96 (6.87 per 10,000 residents; median 2.96).
weaknesses: Education index is below the median at 38, with 2.73 schools per 10,000 residents against a median of 3.43 (tehsil index 38; median 49).
Park density is lower than the median at 7.10 per 10,000 residents, whereas the median is 10.04 (7.10 per 10,000 residents; median 10.04).
Affordability index is low at 29, indicating higher property prices compared to the median of 50 (elcatanliq index 29; median 50).
best_for: Professionals seeking central locations with established metro and bus connectivity.
Buyers looking for commercial properties and high density of retail services.
watch_out: Surface data for 34.7% of roads is unknown, despite the 100% paved share among known surfaces.
Land prices are mock-based at AZN 50,000/sot and should not be used for final financial decisions.
confidence_note: OSM coverage is high and per capita data is reliable. Apartment prices are based on samples, while land prices are mock values.
